newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast products prices stall late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast products prices stall late.

text.p: U.S. West Coast products prices stalled late with few trades done and buyers absent from the market.
NYMEX November crude settled 20 cents lower at $25.42 a barrel -- failing to break through the new post-Gulf War high of $25.72 reached overnight.
Expensive crude futures kept refiners out of the market because of fears of falling margins.
"Crude (futures) is the only thing keeping our market from totally falling out of bed," one broker said.
But sellers refused to cut offers because they saw further upside in crude despite Tuesday's slight correction.
Low sulphur diesel stayed 71.50/72 cents a gallon. A parcel of jet fuel was heard done at 67.50 cents, one cent below yesterday's average price.
Los Angeles CARB regular gasoline flattened at 68/69 cents a gallon, after an early rise lifted the product for the first time in nearly a week.
